'Servitisation' is about turning products into services - directly relevant to an engineer moving into marketing. Wave 2 should run Twente's online eligibility check with the client's 300-ECTS Software Engineering diploma; a positive result would make this the best Dutch fit despite the unverified price.

program_name: Management & Marketing (M.Sc.) - Master of Science in Management & Marketing
institution: Freie Universitat Berlin, Fachbereich Wirtschaftswissenschaft
english_level_required: English at B2 (CEFR) or equivalent. SEPARATELY, applicants whose first degree was not taught in German must pass the DSH (Deutsche Sprachprufung fur den Hochschulzugang) or an accepted equivalent - German proficiency is OBLIGATORY.
ects: TBC (4 semesters; standard German M.Sc. = 120 ECTS, not stated on the page)
tuition_notes: NO TUITION FEES. Official FU page: 'Students do not pay any tuition fees, the university only charges semester fees and contributions each semester.' The FU FAQ page for this programme quotes a semester fee of approximately 300 EUR (that page returned HTTP 503 on the attempt to open it directly, so the exact current figure is TBC). Semester fee typically includes the Berlin public-transport semester ticket.
application_deadline: 31 May (all admission requirements must be fully met and submitted by this date)
entry_requirements_summary: Bachelor's degree in BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION or an equivalent German or foreign degree, WITH a minimum of 12 credit points in accounting and/or taxation AND a minimum of 12 credit points in mathematics, statistics and/or empirical research methods.
scholarship_names: TBC - no programme-level scholarship published; DAAD and Deutschlandstipendium are the usual external routes
red_flags: TWO HARD GATES. (1) DSH-level GERMAN is obligatory for the client - a multi-year language investment, and German is disprefered per the brief. (2) The entry rule demands a BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION bachelor plus 12 CP in accounting/taxation; a Software Engineering diploma clears the 12 CP maths/statistics half comfortably but has no accounting content at all. Exact semester fee not confirmed (FAQ page 503).
fit_notes: ZERO TUITION at a top German research university, which is exactly the funding-first ideal - and the reason to keep it despite the barriers. The 12 CP maths/statistics requirement is trivially satisfied by a 300-ECTS engineering diploma; the accounting requirement is the real blocker and could in principle be closed with a short accounting course before applying. 4 semesters (2 years) means two years of Berlin living costs with no tuition. Language tag: DE+EN - takes the Wave 4 German penalty, not exclusion.

program_name: Marketing Management (M.A.)
institution: Hochschule fur Wirtschaft und Recht Berlin (HWR Berlin / Berlin School of Economics and Law)
language_of_instruction: German and English (approximately half the modules taught in English)
english_level_required: Advanced B2 level: TOEFL iBT minimum 83; IELTS minimum 6.0; TOEIC Four Skills minimum 1200; Cambridge English Scale minimum 170; PTE Academic 67; Oxford Test of English 126. Waived if at least two semesters were previously studied in English, or with a GMAT / GMAT Focus score.
tuition_notes: Official HWR page states tuition fees: NONE ('Keine'). Only the semester contribution (Semesterbeitrag) applies - the page links to the current amount rather than printing it; HWR's semester contribution is around 300 EUR and includes the Berlin semester transport ticket (exact figure TBC).
application_opens: 15 March (international degree holders, via uni-assist); 15 April (German degree holders)
application_deadline: 15 May (international degree holders, via uni-assist); 15 June (German degree holders)
entry_requirements_summary: Minimum 210 ECTS from a bachelor or equivalent in business/economics; applicants holding only 180 ECTS must add 30 ECTS via an integrated practical semester (extending the degree to 4 semesters). PLUS documented evidence of at least 15 ECTS of MARKETING coursework in the previous degree.
red_flags: TWO ENTRY GATES: (1) a business/economics bachelor is required and (2) at least 15 ECTS of prior MARKETING coursework must be evidenced. A Software Engineering diploma fails both. Half the teaching is in German. uni-assist adds a fee and a document-verification step for a Tunisian degree.
fit_notes: ZERO TUITION plus only ~300 EUR/semester - jointly the cheapest option in the entire path alongside HWR's International Marketing Management (AC-023) and FU Berlin (AC-021). CREDENTIAL WIN: the 210-ECTS entry bar is EXPLICIT and the client's 300-ECTS engineering diploma clears it outright, so he enters the 3-semester (18-month) version rather than the 4-semester one - a saved semester. English proof accepted via GMAT as an alternative, a useful option. The 15 ECTS marketing prerequisite is the one thing to solve; ask HWR whether a certified marketing course can be counted.

program_name: International Marketing Management (M.A.)
institution: Hochschule fur Wirtschaft und Recht Berlin (HWR Berlin / Berlin School of Economics and Law)
english_level_required: CEFR B2 equivalent: TOEFL iBT minimum 83; IELTS minimum 6.0; alternatives listed. No further proof needed if two semesters were previously studied in English.
tuition_notes: Official HWR page states tuition fees: NONE ('Keine'). Only the semester contribution applies (amount linked rather than printed; approximately 300 EUR including the Berlin semester transport ticket - exact figure TBC). Confirmed NOT a fee-paying weiterbildend/continuing-education master - it is a regular consecutive master's.
entry_requirements_summary: Economics/business-related bachelor's or equivalent; minimum 210 ECTS (180-ECTS holders add 30 ECTS via an integrated internship, extending to 4 semesters); evidence of at least 15 ECTS in marketing coursework. At least one year of relevant work experience is advantageous but NOT required. Mandatory internship or study-abroad semester available in the 4-semester variant.
red_flags: Same two entry gates as AC-022: an economics/business bachelor AND at least 15 ECTS of prior marketing coursework. Work experience is 'advantageous', which in practice disadvantages a fresh graduate. uni-assist processing required for a Tunisian degree.
fit_notes: BEST BERLIN OPTION ON PAPER FOR THIS CLIENT: fully ENGLISH-taught (no German needed, so it escapes the Wave 4 German penalty entirely), ZERO TUITION, 90 ECTS in 18 months, and the 210-ECTS bar is explicitly cleared by his 300-ECTS diploma - putting him in the shorter 3-semester track. Combined with Berlin's ~0 tuition this is the strongest cost-to-quality ratio in the path. The whole question is the 15 ECTS marketing prerequisite; that single conversation with HWR admissions should be a Wave 2 priority.

program_name: Master Marketing Management (60 ECTS, English)
institution: IU Internationale Hochschule / IU International University of Applied Sciences
city: Berlin (headquarters) - but this programme is delivered by distance learning only
english_level_required: B2 (CEFR): TOEFL 80+; IELTS 6.0+; Duolingo 95+; Cambridge Certificate grade B minimum
tuition_notes: Full-time (12 months) 676-729 EUR/month per the official IU page; 12 x 676 = 8112 EUR at the lower monthly rate (upper rate 729 x 12 = 8748 EUR). Part-time I (18 months) 534-569 EUR/month; Part-time II (24 months) 423-449 EUR/month. A promotional discount of 1444 EUR was advertised. No separate non-EU rate published.
intake_2027_confirmed: yes - rolling enrolment, 'start any time on your preferred date'
entry_requirements_summary: A completed undergraduate degree with a MINIMUM OF 240 ECTS and a final grade of 'satisfactory' or equivalent, PLUS at least one year of qualified professional experience gained after completing the bachelor's. Engineering degrees qualify as acceptable undergraduate degrees.
scholarship_names: IU scholarships referenced but not named or quantified on the page
red_flags: DISTANCE LEARNING ONLY - '100% flexible', 'no mandatory attendance', online exams. A distance programme does NOT support a Tunisian student residence visa for Germany, so this cannot deliver the client's stated goal of moving to Europe. No Berlin on-campus option exists for this particular 60-ECTS English variant. Requires ONE YEAR OF POST-BACHELOR WORK EXPERIENCE, which the client (final-year student) does not have. Accreditation is 'state-approved' (staatlich anerkannt) with ZFU distance-learning registration 1151223 and an AR-Siegel - a real accredited degree, but a distance one.
fit_notes: Logged for completeness and because it is the ONLY programme in this entire path whose official text explicitly says ENGINEERING DEGREES QUALIFY and whose stated 240-ECTS entry bar is directly cleared by the client's 300-ECTS diploma (brief rule: 300 > 240, he qualifies). At ~8100 EUR it also undercuts every Dutch option. But the work-experience clause and the distance-only delivery make it a fallback/insurance option at best, not a relocation route. Could be revisited if the client ever wants to study while continuing to work in Tunisia.
